solution: Operations 2 and 3 never introduce a new magnitude: after the last assignment (or the initial value) with base x, negation flips the sign and clamping is a no-op on a non-negative value but kills a negative one to 0 permanently, so the cell's value is always x, -x or 0 and its history is a sequence of runs. Build a lazy segment tree over positions whose lazy tag is a composable summary of a whole block of operations rather than a single one; since a cell can only ever hold -1, 0 or 1, a tag simply tabulates, for each of those three possible incoming values, the max-subarray tuple (sum, best prefix, best suffix, best subarray) of the versions the tag spans together with the resulting value, so tags compose in O(1) by table lookup. Standard lazy propagation guarantees that a node's pending tag is chronologically later than every pending tag below it, so composing root-to-leaf is exactly time order; a query pushes the path down, applies the leaf's tag to the leaf's concrete tuple, and appends a run of the current value for the versions since the cell was last touched. The answer is the tuple's best field, which is the Kadane merge over the whole version history. The encoding by lastans forces this to be online. Total O((n + q) log n) time and O(n) memory.

notes: Verified: I wrote a brute force and an implementation of the tag-composition segment tree above; both reproduce the official sample exactly, and they agree on 6300 random small tests (values restricted to {-1,0,1}, including deep trees), with internal invariants asserted. The statement is complete, not truncated. Vocabulary gaps: there is no 'kadane' or 'maximum-subarray-sum' label (the corpus already carries ad-hoc slugs for it, e.g. cses-1190 'maximum-subarray-sum' and cses-3226 'range-maximum-subarray-sum'), so I used 'dynamic-programming' as the closest real label and lean on the statement_summary's wording for lexical recall; there is also no label for 'lazy tag is a composable function/monoid over a block of operations', which is the actual idea, nor for 'forced online by answer-encoded queries'. 'brute-force' is listed because the easy version's whole simplification is tabulating the tag over all three possible cell values, which is also what the judge's 'brute force' tag refers to; it is not brute force in the sense of an exhaustive search over the input. Deliberately NOT labelled offline-queries (the lastans encoding forbids offline) or persistent-segment-tree (the statement's 'versions' are a red herring; no persistence is needed). See the notes on E2 for how the two versions differ.
